summary: Independent review retains 19 nonduplicate outgoing links and seven qualified overlaps. Two mathematically accepted Gabriel inputs are kept in the QuiverRepresentations packet and referenced here. Corrected root-lattice, closed-chamber and triality requests to reuse pinned library declarations. All six own stages were spot-checked across 218 roadmaps and 2,007 stages; 217 partner records now include the five additions since the original screen. No new dependency or whole-roadmap merge is proposed.

provenance.libraryAssessment: Not undertaken. Declaration names in evidence are roadmap commitments, not claims verified at the pinned library baseline.
provenance.confidencePolicy: The job-specific METHOD 3 is used: explicit when a text names the other roadmap/stage; inferred for a matched but unnamed output/use. Both endpoint passages are supplied in every case.

overlaps.detail: RootSystems’ scope excludes the general root/weight/coroot/coweight lattices, fundamental weights, dominant integral weights and rho, assigning them to LieHighestWeight. LieHighestWeight’s conventions and Layers 1–2 instead assign the abstract lattice X to RootSystems. Layer 6’s concrete simply connected coordinate lattices do not resolve that general ownership contradiction.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the named finite-type coordinate data with RootSystems and the general highest-weight lattice dictionary with LieHighestWeight, correcting the mutual README import claims. Reuse Mathlib RootPairing.rootSpan and corootSpan at Z and Base.toWeightBasisInt (and the flipped version) instead of defining root/coroot lattices again. The latter is a basis of the root lattice, not a basis of fundamental weights. Audit the remaining weight/coweight, fundamental-weight, rho and real-realization interfaces declaration by declaration before assigning missing comparison work. Compare with the already pinned finite-type coordinate datum; no return dependency on representation classification.

overlaps.detail: Both discuss classical root data, but the finite semisimple types do not supply GL_n’s central character lattice. ClassicalGroups currently names a GL_n root datum from RootSystems even though that provider is not in RootSystems’ stated scope.
overlaps.proposal: ClassicalGroups Layer 3 owns the diagonal-torus datum X=Z^n, roots e_i-e_j, Weyl permutations and central-character comparison. Compare its semisimple quotient with the pinned A_(n-1) model and its restriction to SL_n with weights modulo the diagonal vector. Reuse RootSystems for finite-type matrices and chamber inequalities; keep connected SO/Sp and disconnected O representation problems separate. Coordinate the general lattice unit with LieHighestWeight rather than duplicating it.

overlaps.detail: Both develop reflections and positive-root arguments, but QuiverRepresentations Layer 4 covers arbitrary finite acyclic quivers while RootSystems Layers 1–2 are finite reduced crystallographic. Moreover an arbitrary height-lowering simple reflection is not a sink-admissible lowering for a fixed orientation.
overlaps.proposal: Keep kernel/cokernel reflection functors and dimension-vector reflection formulas in QuiverRepresentations without a finite-type assumption. Add an explicitly finite-ADE comparison unit using the existing root-system Coxeter action. Put the sink-admissible descent/sequence lemma in QuiverRepresentations Layer 5. General Kac–Moody or indefinite Coxeter realizations require a separate supplier; do not claim RootSystems supplies them.

overlaps.detail: Both use positive chambers, but the consumer explicitly allows nonreduced restricted root systems and the supplier explicitly assumes reducedness. Neither text currently states the comparison that would justify an unconditional chamber edge.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the LieGroups-owned comparison from a possibly nonreduced restricted system to a reduced subsystem, with matching hyperplanes, Weyl action and chamber cones, separate from root multiplicities and KAK. Closed-boundary uniqueness itself is already available at the programme pin: TauCeti.eq_of_mem_orbit_of_mem_dominantChamber and existsUnique_mem_orbit_inter_dominantChamber in FundamentalDomain.lean. Import them after establishing the reduced-system comparison and their finite/crystallographic/reduced hypotheses (including the flipped pairing); do not build another uniqueness theorem or infer the comparison from the word chamber.

overlaps.detail: The source README does not list the complete D4 diagram-automorphism theorem, but the programme pin already supplies the numbered three-cycle, exact order three, Cartan preservation and a general lift to the pinned simply connected integral datum. The historical extraction request is therefore stale at the root-data level. CFSG and Spin must share this existing interface; group-level comparison remains separate.
overlaps.proposal: Reuse TauCeti.trialityPermD4, orderOf_trialityPermD4 and cartanMatrix_D4_trialityPermD4 from DiagramPermutations.lean. Apply DynkinType.diagramAut to that diagram symmetry; diagramAut_weightMap gives the fundamental-weight coordinate action, diagramAut_pow_eq_one gives the cube relation, and diagramAut_eq_one_iff plus the nontrivial three-cycle proves nontriviality (hence exact order three). These are pinned library imports, not a new extraction job. The lift to a pinned group scheme and transport to the Clifford Spin carrier remain their owners’ separate obligations. The data-only RootSystems6 -> Spin8 link already exists in the Spin packet and is not duplicated or edited by this review.

overlaps.detail: The root-system realization and lattice acceptance calculations both use ADE coordinates, especially E8. RootSystems’ E8 coordinate construction and IntegralLattices’ D8+ gluing/isometry must not be made mutually prerequisite.
overlaps.proposal: Use one explicit numbered coordinate/Cartan-data interface at the RootSystems boundary. Its primitive E8 coordinate/root checks must not use the downstream discriminant-form classification. IntegralLattices owns full integral submodules, duals, half-norm forms, D8+ gluing and the explicit Gram isometry. Where completed lattice code already supplies primitive coordinates, verify its pinned declaration and extract only that independent prefix, rather than adding a reverse dependency on the whole lattice stage. The programme pin already contains DynkinType.simplyConnectedRootDatum and its numbered base in SimplyConnectedRootDatum/Assembly.lean; consume the verified named datum rather than scheduling another coordinate carrier. A separate discriminant/gluing implementation is not asserted present by that check.

overlaps.detail: The oriented-E8 acceptance example compares a symmetrized Ext-Euler matrix with a root-system Gram matrix. The composition-factor Cartan matrix and nonsymmetric Euler matrix are not themselves root-system Cartan matrices. This example does not make generic K0/Ext-Euler theory depend on finite-type classification.
overlaps.proposal: Keep categorical Ext-Euler descent in GrothendieckEulerForms and quiver dimension-vector formulas in QuiverRepresentations. Pin a separate E8 example comparison with the existing numbered root Gram matrix; check E=I-A and E+E^T=2I-(A+A^T), with the left-module transpose convention. Do not introduce a root-classification dependency on the general Euler-form stage just to run this acceptance example.
